Review operational AI See AI proof Builderz focuses on technically constrained Solana applications, infrastructure integrations, operational AI agent systems, and reliability work. Engagements start with architecture, integration risk, acceptance criteria, and operating ownership rather than a broad feature list. What can I buy from Builderz? Builderz has three entry points: an architecture and delivery sprint for $3K-$5K, a production build for $10K-$40K, and a reliability and rescue sprint for $5K-$15K. Final scope and price are confirmed after qualification. What does an architecture and delivery sprint include? The sprint produces a scoped problem statement, architecture, integration map, risk register, acceptance criteria, technical plan, and build estimate. It is designed for teams that need decision-grade clarity before funding implementation. What qualifies as a production build? A production build can cover a Solana application, infrastructure integration, operational AI agent system, or product engineering scope. The proposal defines milestones, owner, acceptance criteria, exclusions, payment schedule, and change control. When should a team use the reliability and rescue sprint? Use it when an existing system has recurring failures, missing tests or observability, delivery drift, or a blocked launch. Builderz reproduces the failure, maps the risk, and stabilizes the highest-priority paths. How does project qualification work? Submit the project brief at builderz.dev/contact. Builderz reviews the problem, service fit, approved budget, urgency, decision authority, and technical context. Credible fits move to a 30-minute scoping call.
